To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the quantitative T1 and T1, T1 and PD, and T2 and PD-weighted values of regular anatomically defined structures of cerebrums (Group 1) and brainstem and cerebellum (Group2) can be used to differentiate these structures and that the temperature dependence of T1 values is mainly observed.
the post-mortem magnetic relaxation properties of brain structures were quantified and correlated with body temperatures.

quantitative T1, quantitative T2, and quantitative PD values of regular brain structures can be assessed in a post-mortem 1,5T MR quantitation sequence, and that the assessed values can be used to differentiate between the structures.
In summary, our research is concerned with
post-mortem 1,5 Tesla MRI of the human brain and its quantification.
a basic study on the quantitative assessment of regular anatomical structures of the brain in post-mortem 1,5T magnetic resonance imaging.
the development of an MR quantification sequence and its application to post-mortem MR imaging.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the quantitative MR parameters T1, T1/T2, and T2/PD are useful to differentiate between anatomical brain structures in post-mortem MR.

the quantitative T1 and T3 relaxation times and proton densities of the anatomical brain structures investigated here are suitable for the differentiation between the investigated anatomically distinct structures and for the assessment of temperature-dependent changes.
the investigated structures of cerebrums and brainstem/cerellum could be characterized by a combination of their quantitatively determined T1, T 2 and PD values.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the post-mortem MRI quantification of regular brain structures is possible and the quantitative values of the investigated anatomical structures can be used to characterize them.
we were able to characterize regular anatomical brain tissues based on their quantitative T1 and T1 values.
post-mortem 1,5T MR quantifications of regular anatomical structures in the brain can be used as reference values for the detection of brain pathologies or lesions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
MR-quantification of regular anatomics structures is possible at 1.5 T.
post-mortem MR-quantification of regular anatomics structures can be performed and that the quantitative values of these structures depend on the body temperature.
MR quantification can be used to differentiate between different brain structures.
